findings.title: `auto_memory` property has no `None` guard while its sibling does
findings.description:
```python
@property
def auto_memory(self) -> bool:
    """Whether this session's clients load Claude Code auto-memory."""
    return AUTO_MEMORY_DISABLE_ENV not in self.base_options.env
```

`setting_sources`, two lines above, explicitly handles the `None` case (`return None if sources is None else list(sources)`); `auto_memory` does not. `SDKExecutionSession` is a public dataclass requiring only `client` and `base_options`, and both test helpers construct it from `ClaudeAgentOptions(cwd=".", permission_mode="bypassPermissions")` with no `env` (`tests/pipeline/conftest.py#scripted_session`, `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py#_make_options`). If `ClaudeAgentOptions.env` defaults to `None` — which the `base_env: Mapping[str, str] | None` parameter of `sdk_settings_options` and the `# type: ignore[arg-type]` on `kwargs.get("env")` in `provider.py#create_agent` both hint at — this raises `TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not iterable` rather than returning a value.

Today `open_pipeline_session` is the only production constructor and it always passes a dict, so this is latent rather than live. It is also untested on that path: `tests/pipeline/actions/test_dispatch_session.py` sets `session.auto_memory = True` on an `AsyncMock(spec=SDKExecutionSession)`, so the real property body is never exercised with `env=None`. A `return not self.base_options.env or AUTO_MEMORY_DISABLE_ENV not in self.base_options.env` (or a `(self.base_options.env or {})` guard) plus one test would close it.

findings.title: `env` is now set on every SDK spawn, including as `{}` on the default pipeline path
findings.description:
The diff replaces the previous conditional merge with:

```python
settings = sdk_settings_options(config.setting_sources or [], auto_memory=config.auto_memory, base_env=kwargs.get("env"))
kwargs["env"] = settings["env"]
```

This is a real change of shape, not only of content. Before, `kwargs["env"]` existed only when `config.setting_sources == []` (the PR-review path); now an `env` key is always present. `open_pipeline_session` does the same (`env=settings["env"]`), and with `pipeline.auto_memory` at its `True` default and `pipeline.user_settings` at `False`, `sdk_settings_options` returns `env == {}`. So the default pipeline SDK session and the default one-shot pipeline dispatch now pass an **empty but present** mapping where the key was previously absent.

Whether that is equivalent depends on the SDK's merge semantics, and the SDK is not in this repository, so I could not verify it — I am flagging it rather than asserting it. If `ClaudeAgentOptions.env` is merged over `os.environ` the change is inert; if a supplied mapping is treated as the complete subprocess environment, the default pipeline path spawns the CLI without `PATH` and fails immediately. The existing tests assert only on the *contents* of `options.env` (`tests/providers/sdk/test_settings.py`, `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py#test_builder_applies_policy`); none establishes that a spawn with `env={}` still works. One assertion against the installed SDK's merge behavior (or a single smoke spawn) converts this from an open question into a fact.

Note also that the `# type: ignore[arg-type]` on `kwargs.get("env")` is now the only thing standing between the call and the type checker; `sdk_settings_options` accepts `Mapping[str, str] | None` but the `<object>` value from `kwargs` is being passed unvalidated.

findings.title: `docs/TEMPLATES.md` still documents `setting_sources: null` as "no project settings loaded"
findings.description:
`_resolve_setting_sources` now resolves an absent **or null** key to `REVIEW_SETTING_SOURCES = ("project",)`, and the built-in `arch` and `tasks` templates were changed from `setting_sources is None` to `["project"]` (asserted in `tests/review/test_builtin_arch.py`, `tests/review/test_builtin_tasks.py`, and `tests/review/test_templates.py#TestSettingSourcesResolution`). The author-facing guide was not updated and now contradicts the loader in three places:

- line 31: `setting_sources: null | [string]` / `# null: no project settings loaded`
- line 128: the worked example ends with `setting_sources: null`
- line 154: "arch … Does not load project settings (`setting_sources: null`)"

After this change a template that omits the key (or sets it to `null`) **does** load `.claude/settings.json` and `CLAUDE.md` from its `cwd`. For `arch` and `tasks` that is the intended new behavior, but a reader following this guide to author a custom template would be told the opposite of what the code does — and the reason `null` was load-bearing (slice 382 D8, untrusted-cwd isolation for PR reviews) makes the distinction worth stating explicitly rather than silently inverting.

findings.title: The resume-seed log now fires where no session exists to seed
findings.description:
The refactor moved the state load out of the `start_from is not None and sdk_session is not None` guard. `_load_resume_seed` now runs for *every* resumed run, including prompt-only runs (`ExecutionMode.PROMPT_ONLY`, where `run.py` passes `from_step` and no session). In that case it reads the state file, finds the applicable `CompactSummary`, emits

```
executor: resuming at step %d; seeding session from compact summary %s
```

and returns text that `execute_pipeline` then discards, because `sdk_session is None` means neither the rotate branch nor `_connect_lazy_session` consumes it. The operator sees an INFO line claiming a seed that never happened. Moving the log into the two places that actually seed (the rotate branch and `_connect_lazy_session`) would make the signal truthful; the computation itself is cheap enough that leaving it is fine.

findings.title: Seed framing is now applied exactly once
findings.description: Verified against the underlying files rather than the hunk: `_execute_restore` no longer imports or calls `frame_summary_for_seed` and passes raw text to `seed_context`, and `_reconnect` routes through `_seeded_options`, which is the only caller of `frame_summary_for_seed`. `tests/pipeline/actions/test_summary.py#test_restore_frames_summary_exactly_once` pins this by counting `_SEED_FRAMING_PREFIX` occurrences in the new client's `system_prompt["append"]`, which is the right assertion for the defect (a doubled frame) rather than for the implementation. The companion assertions that the rotated client received no `query` cover the #162 safety property.

structured_findings.summary: `auto_memory` property has no `None` guard while its sibling does
`env` is now set on every SDK spawn, including as `{}` on the default pipeline path
`docs/TEMPLATES.md` still documents `setting_sources: null` as "no project settings loaded"
The resume-seed log now fires where no session exists to seed
Seed framing is now applied exactly once
